text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: KV prefix hit-rate collapse detected for tenant `bluecrest-prod` in vpc `vpc-bluecrest` (enterprise). Symptoms: prefix hitrate dropped 92% -> 6% over 5m, KV evictions spiked, 95p latency x3, 502/504 error spike. Auto-pager triggered to #incidents and oncall.

maya (oncall): I'm on it, reading the graphs now. Paging infra + SRE. @luca can you take infra lead? @kevin can you triage KV logs and confirm whether this is pollution vs bug?

luca (infra): taking lead. Looking at prefix heatmap — tons of unique prefixes from the last hour, with many short-lived keys. Looks like a migration/bulk write pattern from Bluecrest. Hot prefixes sample (top keys by evicts): `user/bluecrest-prod/session/*`, `prefs/bluecrest-prod/tmp/*`, `migrate/bluecrest-temp/*`.

kevin (sre): I see repeated writes with TTL=0 from the customer's API agent in logs (same IPs). Prefetch workers are aggressively seeding those prefixes which is thrashing the tenant KV cache. Also seeing KV reclaims at ~95% capacity. Immediate mitigations to consider: 1) throttle/disable prefetch for tenant, 2) enable stronger prefix TTLs, 3) move tenant to isolated dedicated pool if hitrate doesn't recover.

sam (eng-runtime): We have a tenant-scoped prefetch flag we can flip without redeploying runtime. Config path is `tenant_cache.override["bluecrest-prod"]`. Setting `prefetch:false` should stop seeding.

kevin (sre): I'll perform the tenant prefetch disable via control-plane -- doing a canary toggle against a single host first.

kevin (sre): RUNBOOK COMMAND (control plane API):
```
curl -X POST "https://control-plane.internal/tenants/bluecrest-prod/cache-override" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $CP_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"prefetch": false, "note":"mitigate prefix pollution 2061234567"}'
```

ops-bot: Runbook step executed: `cache-override` request received (request_id=cp-req-8a3f). Will apply to one host as canary.

luca (infra): Canary applied to host runtime-34. Observing metrics: eviction rate for that host down ~60% within 90s. Aggregated tenant eviction rate trending down.

kevin (sre): Rolling change to control-plane for full tenant: applying now. Expected stabilization window 5-10m. After disabling prefetch we should see existing keys decay and hitrate recover as hot set stabilizes.

luca (infra): Full toggle applied across vpc-bluecrest. Immediate telemetry: prefix hitrate 6% -> 38% in 4 minutes, 95p latency dropping ~45%. Error rate falling. :white_check_mark:

eli (acct): On a call with Bluecrest now. They report intermittent timeouts on their /generate endpoint. They want an ETA and a short write-up I can send. TL;DR for customer: we identified aggressive background migration seeding new prefixes causing cache thrash; we've temporarily disabled prefetch for your tenant and are monitoring; recommended that you pause the migration job and we will coordinate a safer rollout with TTLs and rate-limits.

maya (oncall): Good. @eli use this message to send to customer:

"Bluecrest team — we temporarily disabled tenant prefetch to stop cache pollution and are monitoring recovery. Expected stabilization within 15 minutes. Please pause any concurrent migration jobs that write large numbers of short-lived keys. We will follow up with root cause and prevention steps. - Redwood Inference Ops"

kevin (sre): Follow-ups and next steps I own:
- Create per-tenant prefetch rate-limit (short term) and a config guard that denies prefetch when new-prefix/sec > 30% of baseline.
- Add alert: unknown-prefix/sec > threshold => auto-disable prefetch and notify.
- Schedule dedicated-pool move playbook if recovery fails.
- Run postmortem and tag the customer mitigation steps.

sam (eng-runtime): I'll create a config PR for the prefetch rate-limiter and a canary test harness for tenant traffic patterns. Will coordinate with testing team; ETA PR in 2 business days.

eli (acct): Customer paused their migration. They've asked for logs showing impact — sharing a sanitized graph and the timeline now. They want a follow-up call tomorrow for rollout strategy.

maya (oncall): Handoff: @luca will remain incident lead until postmortem is posted. I'll stay looped for severity sign-off. Current status = degraded -> recovering. Continue monitoring for 1h and keep this thread updated. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

luca (infra): Adding a short-term safety rule to vpc control-plane: if tenant new-prefix/sec > 1000 then auto-disable prefetch and scale down prefetch workers. Applying now.

ops-bot: Automation performed: safety rule applied (rule_id=r-772b). Notification sent to infra and SRE.

kevin (sre): Notes for postmortem:
- Root cause: customer migration produced a high cardinality of short-lived prefixes that walked the eviction policy causing cold miss storm.
- Contributing factor: prefetch aggressively seeding new prefixes with no backpressure or per-tenant rate limits.
- Immediate mitigation: disabled tenant prefetch; applied safety rule; customer paused migration.
- Long-term mitigation: per-tenant rate limits, alerting, dedicated-pool migration playbook, and improved docs for tenant migration best practices.

eli (acct): Bluecrest thanks the team and will coordinate a safer rollout with us tomorrow. They requested a short blameless RCA and steps to avoid recurrence.

maya (oncall): Closing notes: incident severity reduced to P2, monitoring window in progress. Please file incident record + postmortem in the incident tracker and link here. If anything regresses, re-open the thread and tag @oncall. :white_check_mark:

ops-bot: Incident 2061234567 status changed: RESOLVED -> MONITORING. Postmortem template created at /docs/incidents/2061234567-postmortem (internal).

maya (oncall): thanks team — great coordinated response.
